findings.summary: Honours prefers-color-scheme: a usable dark mode exists and is driven by the user's preference (color-scheme / prefers-color-scheme / light-dark()), not hard-coded light only.
findings.evidence: The preference probe found rootClass="dark" under both emulated light and dark, computed root color-scheme "normal", no prefers-color-scheme or prefers-contrast CSS, and three running animations under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark, derive theme tokens from user preference, add forced-colors/contrast treatment, and stop non-essential animations under reduced motion.

findings.summary: Honours prefers-reduced-motion: non-essential animations and auto-advance are reduced or removed when the user asks for less motion.
findings.evidence: The preference probe found rootClass="dark" under both emulated light and dark, computed root color-scheme "normal", no prefers-color-scheme or prefers-contrast CSS, and three running animations under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

findings.summary: Honours prefers-contrast / forced-colors: controls, text and scrollbars remain visible under high-contrast preferences.
findings.evidence: The preference probe found rootClass="dark" under both emulated light and dark, computed root color-scheme "normal", no prefers-color-scheme or prefers-contrast CSS, and three running animations under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

findings.summary: State and route changes use View Transitions (including same-document, cross-document and scroll-driven/staggered) rather than instant, jarring swaps.
findings.evidence: The CSS/API probe found zero view-transition rules across the loaded styles and representative MPA navigation changes pages abruptly.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance meaningful route/state changes with View Transitions while preserving instant navigation as the fallback.

findings.summary: Sticky/affixed UI reacts to scroll state and position (e.g. the new scroll-state(scrolled) query, shrinking headers, progress indicators) so chrome responds to position instead of static or JS-driven toggling.
findings.evidence: The 14,057px mobile page uses static chrome and the CSS probe found no scroll-state/container, anchor positioning, scroll markers, or view-transition cues.
findings.suggestedFix: Add useful scroll-position feedback and use platform positioning/attention cues only where they help users navigate the long catalogue.

findings.summary: Tooltips, popovers and menus use CSS anchor positioning (with fallback positions) so they stay attached and reposition correctly rather than being manually positioned.
findings.evidence: The 14,057px mobile page uses static chrome and the CSS probe found no scroll-state/container, anchor positioning, scroll markers, or view-transition cues.
findings.suggestedFix: Add useful scroll-position feedback and use platform positioning/attention cues only where they help users navigate the long catalogue.

findings.summary: Navigation and in-page jumps guide attention (highlight effects, scroll/carousel markers, directional transitions, drill-down and drawer navigation) so the user can follow where focus moved.
findings.evidence: The 14,057px mobile page uses static chrome and the CSS probe found no scroll-state/container, anchor positioning, scroll markers, or view-transition cues.
findings.suggestedFix: Add useful scroll-position feedback and use platform positioning/attention cues only where they help users navigate the long catalogue.

findings.summary: No intrusive pop-ups, interstitials or banners that obscure content on load; overlays are dismissible and content-first.

findings.suggestedFix: Remove or defer disruptive ad chrome, cap promotions, and rebuild transient/modal UI with popover or dialog and declarative dismissal.

findings.summary: Served over HTTPS with a sensible Content-Security-Policy and secure, SameSite cookies; no mixed content or obvious transport/header smells.
findings.evidence: HTTPS, HSTS, nosniff, SAMEORIGIN, and no exposed secrets were observed, but CSP, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy are absent; GA/Cloudflare analytics load and the sign-in form is password-only with no autocomplete tokens.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a tested CSP plus Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy, minimize analytics, and add autocomplete/passkey-capable authentication.

findings.summary: The page behaves robustly at runtime: overlays and menus never get cut off, DOM state survives moves, background work and async dependencies are sequenced and conditional rather than fragile, and initial visibility state is detected correctly.
findings.evidence: Raw HTML contains 99% of rendered content, but there is no service worker despite an app/manifest surface, custom overlay runtime is fragile, and the tested 404 is a bare nginx response without recovery.
findings.suggestedFix: Add an offline fallback/service worker if the installable app is intentional, make overlays robust, and provide useful 404/network recovery.

findings.summary: Correct lang and dir attributes, logical CSS properties (inline/block) rather than physical left/right, and translation-ready markup so the layout and reading order survive other languages and writing modes.
findings.evidence: html lang="vi" and Vietnamese relative dates are present, but dir is absent and loaded CSS contains 323 physical left/right declarations versus four logical-property declarations despite a language selector.
findings.suggestedFix: Set dir and replace physical left/right CSS with logical inline/block properties; verify each language route.

findings.summary: No deceptive design: no confirmshaming, forced continuity, disguised ads, or nagging consent walls; honest defaults; clear pricing and consent; easy reversal/cancel; predictable, declaratively-wired actions; and no hidden-text tricks (hidden content stays deep-linkable and indexable rather than used to deceive).
findings.evidence: Screenshots show dominant gambling promotions and an overlapping closable ad; login fields lack required/autocomplete metadata and error containers lack live-region semantics, while account links use data-href rather than real href.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove dominant gambling promotions/dark-pattern pressure and implement humane, accessible form validation with real account links.

findings.summary: Images and decorative assets are optimised and served at appropriate resolutions; decorative pseudo-element imagery and heavy decorative images are resolution-optimised rather than oversized.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 1.98MB on initial load, including 1.36MB across seven advertising media requests; eight muted videos autoplay and 57 below-fold images are not natively lazy-loaded.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not autoplay or preload advertising videos; lazy-load below-fold media, right-size assets, and enforce a proportional media/third-party budget.
